cards.label: Clownfish Reef
cards.challenge: Why do clownfish have orange-and-white stripes? Why hide in those wiggly tentacles?
cards.printAnswer: The stripes help them belong on the reef. They hide in a sea anemone. Those tentacles sting other fish, but a clownfish’s slime keeps it safe.

cards.label: Crab Shore
cards.challenge: Why do crabs walk sideways? What’s the shell for?
cards.printAnswer: Their legs bend that way, so sideways is easiest. The shell is armor. When they grow, they crawl out and make a new one.

cards.label: Seahorse Garden
cards.challenge: Why does a seahorse swim upright? Who carries the babies?
cards.printAnswer: An upright body and a holding tail fit in sea grass. The dad carries the eggs in a pouch.

cards.label: Octopus Den
cards.challenge: How does an octopus hide? Why eight arms?
cards.printAnswer: It can change color and squeeze into tiny holes. Eight arms grab food and feel the way.

cards.label: Ray Flats
cards.challenge: Why is a stingray so flat? Where is its mouth?

video.title: Baby bat rays at Monterey Bay Aquarium

cam.camLabel: Reef cam (rays + sharks) at Monterey Bay Aquarium

cards.printAnswer: A flat body hides on the sand. The mouth is on the bottom, so it can eat what it finds there.

cards.label: Jelly Drift
cards.challenge: Why can a jellyfish sting? Does it have a brain?

cam.camLabel: Jelly cam at Monterey Bay Aquarium

cards.printAnswer: The sting catches food. A jellyfish has no brain — just a simple body that drifts and pulses.

cards.label: Sea Star Pool
cards.challenge: How does a sea star eat? What if it loses an arm?
cards.printAnswer: It can push its stomach out onto its food. If it loses an arm, it can often grow a new one.

cards.label: Shark Reef
cards.challenge: Why do sharks have so many teeth? Do they ever sleep?

video.title: Leopard sharks at Monterey Bay Aquarium

cam.camLabel: Shark cam at Monterey Bay Aquarium

cards.printAnswer: Teeth fall out and new ones grow in. Sharks rest, but not like we sleep in a bed.

cards.label: Eel Cave
cards.challenge: Why does an eel look like a snake? Where does it hide, and why?
cards.printAnswer: A long body slips into holes in the reef. It hides to stay safe and to surprise food.

cards.label: Turtle Current
cards.challenge: Why do sea turtles have flippers instead of feet?

video.title: Sea turtles at Monterey Bay Aquarium

cam.camLabel: Open Sea cam at Monterey Bay Aquarium

cards.printAnswer: Flippers are for swimming far. Feet would be better on land, but sea turtles live in the water.

cards.label: Penguin Beach
cards.challenge: Why can’t penguins fly? Why the black-and-white coat?

video.title: African penguins at the San Diego Zoo

cam.camLabel: Penguin cam at the San Diego Zoo

cards.printAnswer: Their wings became flippers for swimming. Dark backs and white bellies help them hide from above and below.

cards.label: Otter Cove
cards.challenge: Why do sea otters float on their backs? Why wrap up in kelp?

video.title: Sea otters hold on in kelp

cam.camLabel: Sea otter cam at Monterey Bay Aquarium

cards.printAnswer: A back-float lets them use their belly like a table. Kelp is an anchor so they don’t drift away while they rest.

cards.label: Whale Shark Hall
cards.challenge: Why is a whale shark so huge if it eats tiny food? Is it a whale?

cam.camLabel: Ocean Voyager cam at Georgia Aquarium

cards.printAnswer: A giant mouth sifts tiny plants and animals from the water. It is a shark, not a whale — the biggest fish in the sea.

cards.label: Cuttlefish Den
cards.challenge: How can a cuttlefish change colors so fast? Why does it do that?

video.title: How a tiny cuttlefish outsmarts a giant

cards.printAnswer: Tiny skin spots open and close like pixels. Colors help it hide, talk, and trick other animals.

cards.label: Puffin Cliff
cards.challenge: How can a puffin fly and also swim? Why the colorful beak?

video.title: Puffin hunts fish to feed a puffling

cards.printAnswer: Short wings work as flippers underwater and as wings in the air. The bright beak helps them find a mate.

cards.label: Manta Wing
cards.challenge: Why is a manta ray so wide and flat? Why visit a cleaning station?

video.title: Manta ray gets a spring clean

cam.camLabel: Ocean Voyager cam at Georgia Aquarium

cards.printAnswer: Wide wings let it glide and scoop tiny food. Little fish nibble parasites off its skin — a spa for a giant.

cards.label: Kelp Forest
cards.challenge: Why does kelp grow so tall so fast? Who hides in this underwater forest?

video.title: Kelp Forest exhibit at Monterey Bay Aquarium

cam.camLabel: Kelp Forest cam at Monterey Bay Aquarium

cards.printAnswer: Sunlight and the surge of waves help it grow. Fish, otters, and crabs hide in the kelp like trees.
